title: Simulation of a Work-Cell Template
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input, and let $x,z$ be finite Boolean words. Let $n,T,t,p,r$ be natural numbers, let $\tau$ be a work-tape index, let $\mathrm{ph}\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, and let $e$ be an eleven-register assignment. Write $S=M.k(2T+1)+(z.length+n)+3$. Assume $r<2T+1$, $t\le T$, the registers of $e$ satisfy $e_{\mathrm{nc}}=n$, $e_z=z.length$, $e_i=tS+\tau(2T+1)+r$, $e_q=0$ when $t=0$ and $e_q=e_i-S$ otherwise, and $e_{\mathrm{lb}}=tS$. Also assume that the truth values of $\mathrm{ph}\ne0$, $\mathrm{ph}=2$, and $\mathrm{ph}\ne4$ agree respectively with those of $1\le r$, $r=T$, and $r+1<2T+1$. Starting at the label for the work cell indexed by $\tau$ and phase $\mathrm{ph}$, with time-zero flag determined by $t=0$, registers $e$, input position $p$, and any prior output word, the counter program reaches the label following that cell template. Its registers are those of $e$ with $i$ replaced by $e_i+1$ and $q$ by $0$ if $t=0$, or by $e_i+1-S$ otherwise; it appends the instruction bits for position $e_i$, in at most $L_{\max}(M)+3$ steps.
